topic: Agricultural Chemical Runoff, Eutrophication, and Ecological Buffer Strips
scientific_summary: Excess synthetic nitrogen (>120 kg N/ha) in combination with high solubility drives deep nitrate leaching into aquatic ecosystems and accelerates soil acidification via base cation depletion. Broad-spectrum organophosphate and neonicotinoid pesticides reduce non-target soil arthropod biomass by up to 55%.

interventions.name: Engineered Riparian Wetland Buffers and Denitrifying Bioreactors
interventions.mechanism: Planting deep-rooted wetland macrophytes (Typha, Phragmites, Salix) creates anoxic root zones populated by denitrifying heterotrophic bacteria that convert dissolved NO3- into inert atmospheric N2 gas before reaching lotic waterways.
citations: Schipper, L. A., et al. (2010). Denitrifying bioreactors-an approach for reducing nitrate loads to receiving waters. Ecological Engineering, 36(11), 1532-1540.
EPA (2020). Riparian buffer width, vegetative cover, and nitrogen removal effectiveness: A review. US EPA Research Report.

interventions.name: Integrated Pest and Pollinator Management (IPPM) with Beetle Banks
interventions.mechanism: Replacing prophylactic chemical sprays with economic injury thresholds and planting raised berms (0.4m high, 1.5m wide) of tussock-forming grasses (e.g., Dactylis glomerata) establishes permanent overwintering refuges for polyphagous predatory Carabidae and Staphylinidae.
citations: Holland, J. M., et al. (2016). Enhancing ecosystem services in farmland: what do beetle banks deliver? Applied Soil Ecology, 100, 102-113.
UNEP (2021). Environmental and Health Impacts of Pesticides and Fertilizers and Ways of Minimizing Them. United Nations Environment Programme, Nairobi.
